analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. No executable code, keys, endpoints or deployment settings changed, so the changed ranges are documentation. Head lines 1495-1505 add the Qwen think-content seed, the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED=0 opt-out and the unchanged fallback for other parser families. Head lines 1553-1586 add streamed auto tool-call behavior: ToolStreamPreparation.makeHandler, name-first fragments, and the response-hash `tool_call` marker per fragment.

Security-relevant claims I checked against the stated design:
- Undeclared or unresolvable tool names are never exposed, and divergence or schema violation after exposure raises a typed tool_choice violation.
- Required or named tool_choice, native-channel families and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS=0 keep release at the engine terminal after validation.
- No documented change weakens the T-008 fail-closed encryption posture or the T-041 prefix-cache posture (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, coordinator-scoped salt). The unchanged context in units 10 and 11 still matches the T-041 description: encrypted SSD tier, cacheSalt scoping, 30-minute TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch.

Integration questions for later review, all outside this doc-only diff and not evidence of a regression:
- Whether the new tool-call streaming code (ToolCallStreaming.swift, SSEParser encodeToolCallsForHash) keeps tool arguments inside the existing per-hop encrypted SSE path.
- Whether partial fragments exposed before frame-close validation could leak content from the provider to the consumer in ways the coordinator does not expect.
- Whether the response-hash change per fragment stays consistent with coordinator verification.

The patch excerpt was truncated, but unit 11 covers head text only up to line 1657. No security finding is supported from the documentation alone.
